title: Raise Each Block to Its Max
statement:
You get an integer array arr and a block size limit k. Cut the array into contiguous blocks, each holding between 1 and k elements. Then, inside every block, replace each element with the largest value of that block.

Return the largest possible sum of the array after this change.

examples.why: Blocks [2] [7, 1] [1, 5] [3] become 2, 7, 7, 5, 5, 3. Each big value lifts a 1 next to it. Pairing the 7 with the 2 instead gives at most 28, and pairing the 5 with the 3 gives 27.
One block of four, all raised to 4.
Blocks of size 1 change nothing, so the answer is the plain sum.

hints: Look at the last block. If it covers the final j elements, what is left is the same problem on a shorter prefix.
Let best[i] be the answer for the first i elements. The last block has length j from 1 to k.
best[i] = max over j of best[i − j] + j · max(arr[i − j … i − 1]). Grow j one step at a time so the block maximum is updated in O(1).

explain.intuition:
A greedy choice like "give the biggest value the widest block" fails, because blocks compete for neighbours. Instead, decide the last block. If it has length j, it contributes j × (its max), and the rest is the best answer for the shorter prefix, which does not care how the last block was chosen.

That gives a 1-D table: best[i] for the first i elements. To fill it, extend the last block leftwards from position i − 1 one element at a time, keeping its running maximum, and try each length up to k.
steps: For i = 1 … n: set mx = 0, and for j = 1 … min(k, i) update mx = max(mx, arr[i − j]).
Candidate: best[i − j] + j · mx. Keep the largest as best[i].
pitfalls: Recomputing the block maximum from scratch for every j, which adds another factor of k.
Off-by-one between "first i elements" and index i: the last block for prefix length i ends at index i − 1.
Assuming bigger blocks are always better. With [1, 2, 3, 4], k = 2 the best is [1, 2] [3, 4] = 12, not a block around the 4 only.

solutions.title: Try every cut recursively
solutions.idea: Choose the length of the first block, recurse on the rest, without caching.

solutions.title: Bottom-up DP over prefixes
solutions.idea: best[i] = max over the last block length j of best[i − j] + j · (block max).

followups: Only the last k entries of best are ever read. Reduce the space to O(k).
Return the block boundaries of one optimal split, not just the sum.
